title: /standup skill: cycle status report for team standup

content.title: /standup skill: cycle status report for team standup
content.summary: A shared skill, /standup, living in ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/, that gathers the user's current-cycle Linear tickets and their own GitHub PRs and renders a skimmable bullet report for twice-weekly team standup. Each line carries the Linear ticket number and link, the Linear title, a short human-readable summary, the GitHub PR number and link, and a precise state (waiting on me, waiting on reviewers with an age tag, approved/ready to merge, draft). The report ends with an evidence-anchored positive theme and a sub-60-word talk track tied to the Linear project or initiative. Output prints to the terminal and is saved as history in Quaestor-Web/docs/standups/, protected from commits and from clean-scaffolding.
content.problem_statement: The user needs a fast, objective, skimmable view of in-review, done, and in-progress work to give a 30-second standup update. Linear titles are sometimes AI-generated and do not convey the core functionality. PRs can fall out of the user's line of sight. The report doubles as a safety net so nothing is missed or overlooked.
content.solution: A /standup skill backed by scripts: a Linear GraphQL fetch script and a GitHub fetch via gh, then a script that merges, classifies review state, computes age tags and theme signals, and diffs against the last saved standup. The model only writes the human summaries, theme wording, and talk track.
decisions: No out-of-band decisions override this design. Report structure follows the user's description: In Review, Done, In Progress, Blockers, overarching theme, then talk track.

Scope is the union of Linear tickets assigned to the user in the active cycle (any status) and the user's GitHub PRs opened, updated, or merged within the cycle window. Every open PR the user authored is included regardless of age. Unmatched items are tagged '(no ticket)' or '(no PR yet)'.

Review state uses four buckets: 🔴 waiting on me (CI failing or unaddressed reviewer feedback, merged into one state); 🟡 waiting on reviewers (first review and re-review merged into one state); 🟢 approved / ready to merge (rare, since the user usually merges before standup); ⚪ draft, listed under In Progress.
Waiting lines carry a duration age tag (e.g. 'waiting 6d') so stale PRs surface as blockers.
Each PR line lists reviewer names.

Report is one line per ticket+PR pair, assuming the user's 1:1 ticket-to-PR workflow. Lines are grouped under parent ticket or epic headers. A ⚠️ flag marks violations (a ticket with multiple PRs) and Linear/GitHub status disagreements.
Linear data is fetched by a script calling Linear's GraphQL API with LINEAR_API_KEY, not via Linear MCP tools, for consistency with the scriptable-code rule.

The Linear script resolves the user by email (eric@standardmetrics.io) and filters by exact assignee id, cross-checks KEY ids found in PR branches/titles against Linear results and fetches any missing ones, and prints a loud warning instead of an empty section if Linear returns nothing while open PRs exist.

LINEAR_API_KEY resolution order: environment variable, else source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env (the same file gxstart uses, reusing the existing 'gxstart' Linear key), else stop with a one-line setup hint. The script never prints or writes the key. No Keychain step.
Output prints to the terminal and is also saved to Quaestor-Web/docs/standups/YYYY-MM-DD.md.

Standup history must never be committed: add an explicit 'docs/standups/' entry to the Quaestor-Web exclude list in ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/resources/repo-policy.json, and have the skill idempotently add 'docs/standups/' to .git/info/exclude on first run. Never modify .gitignore (admin-owned).
Standup history must not be stored in the dotfiles repo because it is public.
Add docs/standups/ to clean-scaffolding's 'Untouched' list so it is never archived or deleted.

Positive theme is a hybrid: the script computes evidence signals and the model picks framings from an evidence menu (quality bar / no regressions, cross-team collaboration, small reviewable slices, careful spec for accuracy and consistency, steady delivery) but may word the spin freely. Tone is silver-lining; blockers are phrased as 'next step' or 'need eyes on #X from Y', never as complaints.
Report ends with a talk track of 3 to 4 spoken-style lines under 60 words covering shipped, waiting and on whom, next, and theme, tied to the Linear project or initiative.

Done section shows merges since the last saved standup in full with a 🆕 tag, plus a one-line 'Earlier this cycle' summary with links. With no prior saved standup, it falls back to all merges this cycle. The talk track mentions only 🆕 items.
Report covers only the user's own work. No 'waiting on my review' section.
Skill name is /standup with no flags or arguments.
The skill lives in ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/standup/, not in Quaestor-Web.
implementation_decisions: GitHub data is fetched with gh inside a script (gh pr list --author @me plus per-PR reviews, review requests, commits, status checks, and unresolved review thread counts).
Bucket classification, age tags, theme signals, and since-last-standup diffing are computed in scripts. The model writes human summaries, theme wording, and the talk track.
Scripts live in ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/scripts/ with real argument handling, per the global scriptable-code rule.
Since-last-standup cutoff is derived from the most recent file in Quaestor-Web/docs/standups/.

out_of_scope.text: A 'waiting on my review' section for teammates' PRs requesting the user's review.
out_of_scope.rationale: User manages review requests through a different process.

out_of_scope.text: Fetching Linear via Linear MCP tools.
out_of_scope.rationale: User reversed to the script-based GraphQL approach for consistency with the scriptable-code rule.

out_of_scope.text: macOS Keychain storage for the Linear key.

out_of_scope.rationale: User chose terminal plus saved file.
It is maintained by company admins.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Sharing the 'gxstart' Linear API key means revoking or rotating it breaks both gxstart and /standup, and Linear API logs attribute standup calls to the gxstart label. Accepted for personal tooling.
~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env must remain gitignored and untracked in the public dotfiles repo. Verified ignored and untracked on 2026-10-01.
Standup history lives only in the local Quaestor-Web clone via .git/info/exclude, so it is lost on re-clone.

An initial background pull via Linear MCP with an implicit 'me' filter returned zero assigned issues despite PRs referencing KEY-3008 and others. The email-resolved assignee id and PR cross-check guard against this.
Unresolved review threads where the user already replied but pushed no code are classified as waiting on reviewers.
further_notes: Register the skill via /register-skill so tier-advisor tracks it.
The dotfiles repo was on feat/browser-verification at grill time. The skill should be built on its own branch so it does not mix into that work.
The user also asked for today's standup report. Not yet generated at seed time.

tasks.title: Linear standup fetch script
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/scripts/fetch-linear-standup.sh. The script calls Linear GraphQL API to fetch all tickets assigned to the user in the active cycle. Key resolution order: environment variable LINEAR_API_KEY, else source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env (same file gxstart uses), else exit with a one-line setup hint. The script resolves the user by email (eric@standardmetrics.io) to get the exact assignee id, then queries all tickets in the current cycle assigned to that id. It accepts an optional comma-separated list of KEY ids as a positional arg; it fetches any of those missing from the assignee query. If Linear returns no tickets while KEY ids are present in the provided list, it prints a loud warning to stderr instead of an empty section. Outputs a JSON array of {id, key, title, status, url, parentKey, epicKey} objects to stdout. Includes automated tests (bats or bash with fixtures) covering: key resolution order, empty-but-keys-present warning, and correct JSON shape from a mocked curl response.
acceptance_criteria: Script exits 0 and emits valid JSON array to stdout on success
Tests verify key resolution: env var trumps secrets.env; secrets.env trumps exit-with-hint
Tests verify loud stderr warning when Linear returns empty but KEY ids arg is non-empty
Tests mock GraphQL response and assert output shape {id, key, title, status, url, parentKey, epicKey}
Script never prints or writes LINEAR_API_KEY
tasks.summary: Created fetch-linear-standup.sh: resolves user by email, fetches active cycle tickets, supplements with provided KEY ids. 7 test cases, 19 assertions with mocked curl.

tasks.title: GitHub PR fetch script
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/scripts/fetch-github-standup.sh. The script uses gh pr list --author @me --json to list all PRs authored by the user. For each PR it fetches: reviews (reviewer login, state), review requests (requestedReviewers), head branch name, title, body, state, draft flag, createdAt, updatedAt, mergedAt, CI check rollup (success/failure/pending), and unresolved review thread count. Outputs a JSON object to stdout with two fields: prs (array of PR objects) and key_ids (array of Linear ticket key strings extracted from branch names and titles, e.g. KEY-3008). Tests use fixture JSON files to mock gh output and assert the output shape and KEY id extraction logic.
acceptance_criteria: Script exits 0 and emits valid JSON with prs array and key_ids array to stdout
Tests use fixture gh output and assert correct PR object shape
Tests assert KEY id extraction from both branch names and PR titles
CI check rollup state is one of: success, failure, pending, none
Unresolved review thread count is numeric (0 when none)
tasks.summary: Created fetch-github-standup.sh: gh PR fetch emitting prs and key_ids. Fixture-injected via GH_PR_LIST_FIXTURE and GH_PR_THREADS_FIXTURE. 33 assertions pass.

tasks.title: Standup data processing script
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/scripts/build-standup-data.sh. The script accepts two file paths as args: a Linear JSON file and a GitHub JSON file (both produced by T-0033 and T-0034). It pairs tickets to PRs via KEY id matching in branch names and titles. Classifies each PR into four review buckets: red (CI failing or unaddressed reviewer feedback), yellow (waiting on first or re-review), green (approved/ready to merge), white (draft). Computes age tags (waiting Nd) based on PR createdAt or last-activity date. Groups paired items under parent ticket or epic headers. Flags violations with a warning marker: a ticket with multiple PRs, or a Linear status disagreeing with the PR merged state. Diffs against the most recent saved standup in Quaestor-Web/docs/standups/ to determine which merges are new since last standup (done_new) vs earlier this cycle (done_earlier). Computes evidence signals for the positive theme: presence of cross-team reviewers, small PR sizes (file count), CI green ratio, steady delivery count. Outputs one structured JSON object to stdout for model consumption: {in_review, done_new, done_earlier, in_progress, blockers, theme_signals, violations, since_last_standup_cutoff}. Tests cover: bucket classification logic for each state transition, age tag computation, KEY pairing, violation detection, and diff cutoff logic.
acceptance_criteria: Script exits 0 and emits a valid structured JSON object to stdout
Tests verify bucket classification for each of the four states (red/yellow/green/white)
Tests verify age tag computation for PRs of varying ages
Tests verify violation detection for multiple-PR tickets and status disagreements
Tests verify done_new vs done_earlier split against a fixture standup file
Tests verify theme_signals fields are computed from PR data
tasks.summary: Created build-standup-data.sh: pairs PRs to tickets by KEY id, buckets red/yellow/green/white, age tags, violation flags, done_new/done_earlier split by newest standup file, theme_signals. Extended fetch-github-standup.sh with changedFiles.

tasks.title: Standup skill and output rendering
tasks.description: Create the /standup skill at ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/standup/SKILL.md. The skill orchestrates the three scripts: calls fetch-github-standup.sh first to get GitHub PR data and extract KEY ids, then calls fetch-linear-standup.sh with those KEY ids, then pipes both JSON outputs to build-standup-data.sh. The resulting structured JSON is fed to the model, which writes: a one-line human-readable summary for each ticket+PR pair, the positive theme sentence (chosen from evidence menu: quality bar / no regressions, cross-team collaboration, small reviewable slices, careful spec for accuracy and consistency, steady delivery), and the talk track (3-4 spoken-style lines under 60 words covering shipped, waiting and on whom, next, and theme tied to the Linear project or initiative). Output is rendered to the terminal in the prescribed section order: In Review, Done (new merges with a new tag, then one-line Earlier this cycle summary with links), In Progress, Blockers, theme, talk track. The done section falls back to all cycle merges when no prior standup file exists. The rendered report is also saved to Quaestor-Web/docs/standups/YYYY-MM-DD.md (the date is the run date). On first save, the skill idempotently appends docs/standups/ to Quaestor-Web/.git/info/exclude. The skill never modifies .gitignore. Tests: dry-run with fixture JSON inputs that exercises the full render pipeline without real API calls.
acceptance_criteria: Skill file exists at ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/standup/SKILL.md
Dry-run with fixture JSON produces a terminal report with all six sections (In Review, Done, In Progress, Blockers, theme, talk track)
Talk track is 3-4 lines and under 60 words

docs/standups/ is appended to Quaestor-Web/.git/info/exclude on first run (idempotent on subsequent runs)
.gitignore in Quaestor-Web is not modified
Tests use fixture data and do not call Linear GraphQL or gh

tasks.title: Register skill and update infra policy files
tasks.description: Register the standup skill in the shared skill registry and update the two policy files that govern standup history handling. First, invoke /register-skill standup to add the skill to model-tiers.json so tier-advisor and the weekly usage report track it. Second, add a docs/standups/ entry to the Quaestor-Web exclude list in ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/resources/repo-policy.json (the per-repo exclude list that prevents standup history from being committed). Third, locate the clean-scaffolding skill and add docs/standups/ to its Untouched list so it is never archived or deleted by clean-scaffolding runs. Tests verify that model-tiers.json contains a standup entry, that repo-policy.json contains the Quaestor-Web exclude entry, and that the clean-scaffolding Untouched list contains the entry.
